cases.name: api-ripemd160-digest-sum-1024
cases.notes: Closest published code: bitcoin/Ripemd160.Digest.sum finalizes and consumes/locks mutable state; plugin Digest.sum preserves state for repeat finalization and continued writes. Both return the same digest once. Result array-to-Blob conversion is timed. Cost ratio does not imply equivalent state-preservation contracts.

cases.name: api-ripemd160-init-0
cases.notes: Closest published code: bitcoin/Ripemd160.Digest() constructs mutable object state, while plugin init() returns a canonical immutable Blob. Timed constructor only; finalization for empty-state oracle occurs in query. No allocation/representation equivalence is claimed.

cases.name: api-ripemd160-update-1024
cases.notes: Closest published code: bitcoin/Ripemd160.Digest.write mutates its prepared receiver; plugin update returns a new immutable state preserving the input state and validates serialized state. Both append the same bytes to a 17-byte prefix. Required Blob-to-array input conversion is timed; final digest is checked in query. Cost ratio does not imply equivalent mutation/validation contracts.

cases.name: bech32-convert-8to5-n32
cases.notes: Closest published code: exact private convertBits function extracted unchanged from bitcoin0.2.1 Segwit.mo, with attribution and SHA256 pins. Valid 8-to-5 padded conversion matches byte-for-byte; Blob-to-array and array-to-Blob adapters are timed. The plugin additionally validates bit widths and enforces16MiB input/output bounds; published private code assumes valid widths and has no such cap. This is a benchmark-only actor-private extraction, not a public package API.

cases.name: api-blake3-finalizexof
cases.notes: Closest published code composed from two correct public hasherFinalizeSeek calls: bytes13..63 and64..112, concatenated and converted to Blob inside timing. The pinned single call truncates at its first output-block boundary, so it cannot provide100bytes directly. This composition produces identical official-vector output without implementing compression or cryptographic state transitions. Only one1024-byte input chunk is used; this does not repair upstream multi-chunk hashing. State preparation is excluded and finalization preserves its immutable receiver.

cases.name: api-blake3-derivekey
cases.notes: Closest published primitives composed with two-phase domain separation: exported Hasher record/DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT flag hash UTF8context; resulting32-byte key initializes published hasherInitKeyed with exported DERIVE_KEY_MATERIAL flag. All compression, state updates, key decoding and finalization use pinned public functions. The high-level upstream derive_key ignores context and is not used. Official BLAKE3 context/material vectors independently check this bounded composition; context and material each fit a single1024-byte chunk, so no claim is made for broken upstream multi-chunk behavior. The whole derive operation is timed.
